title: Demo names taken from CLI argv are interpolated into filesystem paths without sanitization
evidence:
harness/main.odin:60: "args := os.args[1:]"
harness/main.odin:131: "path := fmt.tprintf("demos/%s.dem", name)"
harness/main.odin:310: "write_log(fmt.tprintf("goldens/%s.log.bin", name), pp.log_write(rc.state, context.temp_allocator))"
harness/goldens.odin:55: "return fmt.tprintf("goldens/%s/%05dms.png", demo, ms)"
detail: A demo name such as `../../x` breaks out of demos/ and goldens/ for both reads (run_demo) and writes (write_log, golden_path). No `../` or absolute-path check exists. Local same-user CLI only, so impact is self-inflicted, not remote.
recommended_fix: Validate demo names before path interpolation: reject names containing '/', '\', '..', or leading '.', or resolve and canonicalize the path and verify it stays under demos/ and goldens/.
